name: netsuite-latam
label: NetSuite Latam Agencies
description: Targets decision-makers at NetSuite implementation agencies and Oracle partners in Latin America. Same staff augmentation proposition as agency-partners, with outreach composed in Spanish.
_note: Latin American counterpart to agency-partners. Focus on consultancies implementing NetSuite and SuiteCommerce for clients in Latam. All messages must be written in neutral Latin American Spanish.
_refresh_note_2026_09_15: Criteria-extractor refresh (via /refresh-criteria, first real extraction pass for this file — generated_from_connections was 0 and generated_at was a hand-authored 2026-06-11 stub before this run, never previously refreshed): reused the same 192-connection pull (get-connections, 16 pages, startIndex 0-180, limit 12, sortBy recentlyAdded, connectedDate 2026-07-16 through 2026-09-15) gathered for the same-day agency-partners refresh, since both files draw from the same LinkedIn account's connections and the extractor's job is to re-read that population through this file's Latam-specific lens. Headline finding: this account's organic connections are overwhelmingly a global/US NetSuite-ecosystem network, not a Latam-dense one — only a handful of connections carry a clear Latam signal (Spanish-language headline, Latam country, or explicit 'en Perú'/'en Latinoamérica' framing), which is expected since Latam density for this criteria is meant to come from this criteria's own targeted searches (Step 2), not from organic connection growth. Findings: (1) reference_companies — added: none existed before (unlike agency-partners, this file had no reference_companies key at all). Added 'Nufocus' on real evidence: two independent connections at the same Peru-based firm both surfaced with explicit platform+partner branding — José Luis Calderón Diaz ('Co-Founder | Director Comercial Nufocus | Oracle NetSuite Alliance Partner – Perú, Latinoamérica y USA') and Omar Magallanes Valdivia ('Delivery Manager en Nufocus | Alliance Partner #1 de Oracle+NetSuite en Perú'). (2) company_type_signals — added 'Alliance Partner' and 'NetSuite Alliance Partner': both Nufocus headlines above use this exact English phrase even inside otherwise-Spanish text (code-switching is common in this professional register), and the existing Spanish-only signals ('Socio NetSuite', 'Partner Oracle') would have missed both. (3) target_roles — no addition. 'Director Comercial' (José Luis Calderón Diaz) and 'Delivery Manager' (Omar Magallanes Valdivia) each appeared once — flagging, not adding, consistent with agency-partners' no-single-instance-evidence practice. Also flagging: Khalita Hicks ('Sales Director | Helping Multinational Companies Expand into LATAM with Oracle NetSuite | NetSuite Localization Expert') is a near-perfect fit for this criteria's proposition despite not being Latam-based herself — 'Sales Director' is already in agency-partners' target_roles (added 2026-08-21) but was never backported here; one instance isn't enough to add unilaterally, but a second independent sighting anywhere should trigger adding it to both files for consistency. (4) target_industries / target_locations: unchanged — no industry/location field returned by get-connections (same gap as agency-partners), and Peru is already covered by the existing target_locations list. (5) search_terms, anti_patterns, excluded_employers, excluded_companies, scoring_weights, classification_thresholds, language: left untouched — no data-driven reason to change any of them this run.
_company_type_signals_note: Must be platform-specific to count toward agency boost. 'Consultora', 'Tecnología', 'Soluciones', 'Digital' alone are not sufficient — they must appear alongside a platform keyword like NetSuite, Oracle, SuiteCommerce, or Shopify.
_target_industries_note: Same as agency-partners. LinkedIn industry field must be combined with platform-specific domain signals — industry alone is not sufficient.
_excluded_employers_note: AOTT sells staff augmentation TO the partner ecosystem, never to the platform vendors themselves. Anyone whose CURRENT employer is a platform vendor is not a lead: they have internal delivery orgs and do not buy external agency capacity. Detect from the headline when company fields are null: 'at Oracle', 'en Oracle', 'at NetSuite', '@ Shopify', 'Oracle Consulting'. Oracle-internal titles like 'Consulting Practice Director' / 'Director de Consultoría en Oracle' are vendor employees, not partner-agency staff. Classify excluded-employer leads as cold and cap score at 25 regardless of seniority — this exclusion overrides company_type_signals and seniority_signals. Do not drop them from output; the operator can rescue from cold. Also cold: mega-SIs (Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, IBM, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Cognizant, Globant) — cap at 40; and in-house IT/ERP leaders at end-user enterprises — cap at 30. The buyer must work at a consultora/agency whose BUSINESS is delivering NetSuite/SuiteCommerce projects for clients.
_excluded_companies_note: Operator feedback 2026-06-09 (SuiteDB), 2026-07-27 (Seibert Consulting Group), 2026-08-06 (AnagramDev), and 2026-08-06 (FullClarity — no fit for AOTT despite being a genuine NetSuite partner), and 2026-09-10 (Techfino — same 'no fit despite scoring well' pattern, also removed from any reference_companies list it appeared in): absolutely no interest in engaging with these agencies under any circumstances — never surface anyone from these firms in any tier, in any criteria. Unlike excluded_employers (surfaced cold), these are dropped entirely at Step 2 — skip the result AND write it to seen.json so it never resurfaces. Detect from headline naming the firm; Seibert Consulting Group's staff may abbreviate as 'SCG' in headlines (e.g. 'at SCG') — treat that alongside any Seibert/NetSuite/Shopify Plus context as the same exclusion. Operator feedback 2026-08-12: N2Lab is now an active AOTT client relationship — exclude from all criteria and never surface as a new lead, regardless of fit.
_search_terms_note: QUERY-BUILDING RULE for Step 2: never pair a bare platform name with a role — 'Oracle consulting' matches Oracle's own Consulting org. Every query must include a partner/implementador/consultora/agency qualifier alongside the platform name so results skew toward people whose employer partners with the platform rather than the vendor's own staff.
